solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Quick gain – throw up after a diet!

blocks.note: a diet is a fast, a period of going without food
a horse that bucks throws its rider up and off

explanation.surface: Someone recommends vomiting after dieting as a quick way to lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the throwing up second, behind the diet. 'Throw up' looks like vomiting, but it is the horse's buck.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a fast buck is an idiom for earning money quickly and often dubiously.

clue.text: Cane remedy for adolescent outbursts

indicators.note: to remedy something is to put it right, so these letters are fixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned headmaster prescribes the cane to cure teenage tantrums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outbursts' suggests temper; here they are eruptions of spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is the skin condition of spots that breaks out mainly on teenagers.

clue.text: see 8ac.
Manufactured item ready for sale is shit?

blocks.note: first meaning: the finished goods a factory turns out
second meaning: what the body finally turns out after digestion

explanation.surface: A cynic sneers that the finished goods coming off the line are rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is shit?' reads as a verdict on quality; it is the second meaning, faeces as the body's final output.
explanation.definitionFit: The end product is the final result of a process, whether in a factory or in the gut.

clue.text: "Cabbie stress" Cyclops had, flower

blocks.note: to tax is to strain or stress
the setter refers to themself, so the setter's name gives I
had shortens to 'd, as in I'd
a river is something that flows, a flow-er

explanation.surface: The setter recounts a cab driver's stress, then drifts off to a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'stress' look like part of the cabbie's words. Flower is the old crossword trick: a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabbie is the informal name for someone who drives a taxi for hire.

clue.text: Mug putting money in the bank – like the actions of politician after ballsing up?

definitions.text: like the actions of politician after ballsing up

blocks.note: mug is slang for face
depositing money is saving it

explanation.surface: A sucker banks his cash, then the clue sneers at politicians covering up their blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a dupe; it is the face. 'Ballsing up' is British slang for making a mess of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Face-saving describes acts meant to preserve dignity or reputation after an embarrassing failure.

clue.text: Deputies such as Prescott's post-dessert treat?

blocks.note: first meaning: assistants who stand in, as a second does in a duel or boxing match
second meaning: further helpings of food after the first plate

explanation.surface: A jibe at John Prescott, Labour's deputy prime minister, for going back for more pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott was Tony Blair's deputy prime minister and famously portly, so he is both a second-in-command and a man who has second helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: Seconds are both supporting deputies and extra helpings of a meal taken after the first.

clue.text: (& 3dn.) Electorate once embracing Gordon's debut – unpleasant after-effects!

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps around another
a debut is a first appearance, so only the opening letter of the name is used

blocks.note: Hanover was an Electorate of the Holy Roman Empire, ruled by an Elector
the opening letter of Gordon, as in Gordon Brown

explanation.surface: A dig at Gordon Brown's arrival at Number 10 leaving a nasty aftertaste for voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electorate' looks like the voters; historically it was a German state such as Hanover, whose ruler helped elect the Emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is the sick feeling after drinking, or any unwelcome legacy from an earlier event.

clue.text: see 25dn.
(& 27ac.) Awful, what peers do with a no.2 (Brown's no.2)

indicators.note: number two in the name means its second letter is the one kept

blocks.note: read as pee-ers, people who pee, and what they do
number two is a childish euphemism for faeces
the second letter of Brown

explanation.surface: Lords in the upper house are mocked for being stuck with Gordon Brown's deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' are members of the House of Lords on the surface; cryptically they are people who pee.
explanation.definitionFit: Piss-poor is coarse British slang meaning extremely bad or of very low quality.

clue.text: Once, Di's last bits of cash grabbed by Charles and mother finally

indicators.note: something grabbed is held tight between the grabber's hands
finally points to the end of each of the two names before it

blocks.note: the final letter of Charles
pence are small coins
the final letter of mother

explanation.surface: Princess Diana's final coins are snatched by Prince Charles and his mother the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Di's last' reads as her final something; it means her last name, which she had only before marrying Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana's maiden surname was Spencer, so it was her family name before she became Princess of Wales.

clue.text: Tarts would hold one in motorised caravan for johns

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another
in places the number inside the vehicle

blocks.note: tarts are pies
RV, recreational vehicle, is a motor home
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Prostitutes entertain clients called johns in a camper van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tarts' and 'johns' set up prostitutes and their customers; really they are pastries and toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: A john is American slang for a lavatory, and a privy is an old word for an outdoor toilet.

clue.text: (& 15ac.) The PM, "pants" according to Obama – such times are very scary

blocks.note: Gordon Brown was the UK prime minister at the time
in American English pants are trousers

explanation.surface: Barack Obama is reported as calling Gordon Brown 'pants', British slang for rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like British slang for useless; to an American it simply means trousers. Brown trousers time is slang for a moment so frightening one might soil oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown trousers is a British idiom for sheer terror, from the fear of losing bowel control.

clue.text: Kissing so, with an erection, copper mounts Joy, topless

indicators.note: in a down clue an erection makes the word stand upright, so it reads from bottom to top
with its top removed, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
elation is great joy

explanation.surface: A smutty scene: a policeman, aroused, climbs on top of a bare-breasted woman named Joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is a policeman in the surface and the metal cryptically; 'mounts' just places it above what follows in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Osculation is the formal or scientific term for the act of kissing.

clue.text: see 13ac.
Do this with Brown and row will ensue

definitions.text: Do this with Brown and row will ensue

blocks.clueFragment: Do this with Brown and row will ensue
blocks.note: surface reading: some action involving Gordon Brown will cause a quarrel
setter's reading: remove the first and last letters of the name and the remaining letters spell the second word

explanation.surface: A warning that some dealing with Gordon Brown is bound to start a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Row looks like a quarrel; it is simply the three letters left when the name loses its head and its end.
explanation.definitionFit: To top and tail is to trim off both ends, as cooks do with beans or gooseberries.

clue.text: Could be Brucie's now kissing butts of Arlene and partner

indicators.note: butts are the back ends, so only the final letter of each name is kept

blocks.note: the present is now
the final letter of Arlene
the final letter of partner

explanation.surface: Bruce Forsyth snogging the backsides of Strictly judge Arlene Phillips and her dance partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Brucie is Bruce Forsyth, long-time host of Strictly Come Dancing, where Arlene Phillips was a judge. 'Kissing' just means touching, so the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruce Forsyth was a television host, an example of someone who fronts a programme.

clue.text: Erection's occurred, but makes a mess of it

blocks.note: first meaning: read as ..., the penis has risen
second meaning: British slang for bungling something

explanation.surface: A man gets aroused but then fumbles the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is the phrase read as cock's up; the second is the British verb to cock up, to botch.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock up is a British slang verb meaning to ruin or bungle a task.

clue.text: Blow lid on useless, naff Conservative leaders – "surplus to requirements"

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so each of the three words gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of useless, naff and Conservative
over means extra, left over beyond what is needed

explanation.surface: An exposé of hopeless, uncool Tory leaders who are no longer needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky or uncool.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow the lid on something is an idiom for exposing it, which is to uncover it.

clue.text: Er, short knight in lacy creation, mud-slinging

indicators.note: a creation is something made up, so these letters are made into a new order
in places the hesitation and the knight inside the reworked letters

blocks.note: taken as written
er and um are both sounds of hesitation
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly describes a little nobleman in a frilly lace outfit being smeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of the knight's height; it marks the abbreviation used in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is the making of false, damaging statements about someone, which is mud-slinging.

clue.text: Windy thing destroying article about "finish of Cameron"

indicators.note: destroying the word breaks it apart so its letters can be rebuilt
the finish is the end, so only the last letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of Cameron

explanation.surface: A long-winded critic tears apart a newspaper piece on David Cameron's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windy thing' sounds like a gasbag politician; it is a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, played by blowing, so a jocular wind thing.

clue.text: Labour's last uncertainty: time for a split

indicators.note: last points to the end of the party name, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of Labour
an if is a doubt or uncertainty, as in ifs and buts
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Doubts in the dying days of the Labour government point to a party split.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift is a break or division, whether in rock or between people.

clue.text: Political body that's no stranger to spin

blocks.note: first meaning: the House of ..., the upper chamber of Parliament
second meaning: ..., the London cricket ground, where spin bowling is a regular sight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' suggests political media management; the second meaning is Lord's, the London cricket ground, where spin bowlers turn the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lords is the short name for Parliament's upper house, and Lord's is the home of English cricket.

clue.text: Shit, shit! Palin's only just started!

indicators.note: something that has only just started has shown just its first letter

blocks.note: poo is a childish word for faeces
the first letter of Palin

explanation.surface: Someone groans in dismay that Sarah Palin is barely into her speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Palin was the 2008 US Republican vice-presidential candidate. The first 'Shit' is the definition; the second is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Poop is an informal, chiefly American word for excrement.

clue.text: Under the table, sex all used up?

blocks.note: first meaning: so drunk as to have slid to the floor
second meaning: it is a slang word for sex

explanation.surface: A drinker ends the night on the floor, too spent for any sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is old slang for sex, so having used it all up leaves you out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of it is slang for being drunk or stoned, too intoxicated to function.

clue.text: Light shining round hole produces ridicule

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the earlier words wrap about the next one

blocks.note: a lamp is a light
a light that is shining is on
O is shaped like a hole

explanation.surface: A torch shone around a hole, perhaps a peephole, leads to mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a satirical attack that holds someone up to ridicule.

clue.text: (& 9dn.) To endure flatulence, pee at the final second

blocks.note: to last is to endure
gas is wind in the gut
pee is the spoken name of the letter P

explanation.surface: Someone holds on through wind and the need to urinate until the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pee' looks like urinating; it is how the letter's name is spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-gasp effort is one made at the very last moment, like a final breath.

clue.text: Gore on recycling can be a bit of a bastard

indicators.note: recycling remakes material into something new, so these letters are reprocessed into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, as in Al Gore

explanation.surface: Al Gore, the environmental campaigner, can be insufferable when lecturing on recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Gore is the former US vice-president known for his climate campaigning.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous giant, and figuratively a cruel, frightening person.

clue.text: see 10dn.
Snooker event well behind? Get lost!

blocks.note: in snooker a kiss is a light touch between two balls
well and my are both exclamations of surprise
behind is the backside, arse in British slang

explanation.surface: A snooker player, well behind in a match, is told to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well behind' reads as trailing badly in the scores; 'well' and 'behind' split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiss my arse is a rude British dismissal, an insult meaning go away.
